- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00 or low) and model forecasts show upward trend, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — cap downward revisions to prevent overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bullish, model often underreacts — adjust forecast upward slightly to reflect market anticipation.  
- In multi-event periods with high bearish sentiment and supply net, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer below forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after auction, model often fails to anticipate — adjust downward by 3–8% in first 5–7 days.
